archetype.name: Playoff Team (shooting-first)
archetype.definition: A Golden State side that wins on the volume and accuracy of its perimeter shooting and its work on the offensive glass, and has to outscore a defense that leaks at the rim to get to the postseason.

report.headline: Shooting and second chances carry a leaky defense; Curry's absence is the test.
report.take:
Seven games in, Golden State looks like a different team from the one that went 37-45 last season and finished 20th on the site. It sits 8th now, with a Net Rtg of 2.9 (12th). The shape of it is lopsided. The offense rates 119.4 points per 100 possessions, 5th in the league, and the defense allows 116.5, 23rd. This is a team that scores its way through games rather than grinding them.

The offense rests on two things. The first is three-point volume and accuracy: a 3PA Rate of 47.2 (5th) and a 3P % of 40 (2nd), well above the league's 34.7. The second is something new for this franchise. Its ORB % of 33.2 leads the league, far above anything in its recent history, where it sat between 22.8 and 27.5. Add an Opp TOV % of 15.7 (3rd) and the Warriors are winning the possession battle, which matters at a slow Pace of 97.1. The wings grade A+, almost entirely because Yaxel Lendeborg has played the most minutes on the roster and posted a 64.5 TS % on a 27.1 USG %. The backcourt grades A-, led by Stephen Curry's 14.9 BPM and 69.1 TS % and by De'Anthony Melton's 70.7 TS %.

The record is honest. W vs Pt Diff is 0, the differential implies the same 4 wins it has, and the recent run came on margin: a 4-1 last five at plus 9 a game, with wins at Denver and Minnesota inside a four-game streak. What the numbers hide is the frontcourt. It grades D-, and opponents shoot 73.1 at the rim, 29th and nearly eight points above the league. The low Opp Rim Rate (6th) suggests the scheme keeps teams out of the paint, but when they get there, nobody stops them. The on-off figures are too noisy in seven games to lean on: Lendeborg at -30.5 and Malevy Leons at +32.5 in 16 minutes tell you about lineup samples, not players.

The immediate problem is availability. Curry and Draymond Green are both listed out, and Gui Santos is day-to-day. Without Curry, the shot creation falls to Brandon Williams, whose 30.4 USG % comes with a 52.8 TS %, and to Lendeborg. The 82-game pace of 47 wins is a reasonable ceiling for a healthy version of this team. The realistic expectation is a winning season built on the offense, unless the rim defense finds an answer.

strengths.title: Elite three-point shooting at volume
strengths.body: The Warriors take nearly half their shots from deep and make 40 percent of them, 2nd in the league and 5.3 points above average. Curry and Melton are the engines; Curry has 22 threes in five games. Volume is a stable trait of this franchise. Accuracy this high is not, since recent seasons ran between 35.6 and 38.5, so expect the efficiency to settle somewhat while the shot profile stays elite.

strengths.title: Winning the possession battle
strengths.body: Golden State leads the league in ORB % at 33.2, nearly six points above average, and forces turnovers at the 3rd-best rate. At a slow pace, extra possessions are worth more. The offensive-rebounding jump is far beyond the 25.8 of last season, so some of it is small-sample. The turnover-forcing is closer to a trait this roster can repeat.

strengths.title: A record backed by margin
strengths.body: There is no close-game luck in this 4-3: W vs Pt Diff is 0, and the differential implies exactly the wins on the board. The last five games ran at plus 9 a game, over six points better than the season. That run included road wins at Denver and Minnesota and a 17-point home win over the Lakers.

concerns.title: No rim protection, soft defensive glass
concerns.body: Opponents shoot 73.1 at the rim, 29th in the league and 7.8 above average, and the Warriors rebound only 70.7 of opponents' misses (22nd). The frontcourt grades D-. Its listed players have combined for 0.6 Win Shares in 572 minutes, while the backcourt has 2.4. Even last season's mediocre defense allowed 67.3 at the rim, so this is worse than the recent baseline, and nothing on the roster suggests a quick fix.

concerns.title: Curry and Green both out
concerns.body: Curry's 14.9 BPM and 34.4 USG % make him the offense's hub, and Green, though quiet as a scorer, runs the frontcourt's playmaking with 36 assists. With both listed out, more creation falls to Williams, who has used a lot of possessions inefficiently. How long the absences last is the biggest variable in the near-term outlook.

concerns.title: Turnovers and a shooting regression
concerns.body: The offense gives the ball away at a TOV % of 14.7, 21st and above the league average. Shooting is masking those lost possessions. If the 40 percent from three drifts toward this team's recent norms, the 5th-ranked offense will lose some of the cushion it needs to cover a bottom-eight defense.

trend.note: Golden State lost its first three games, including a loss at Phoenix, then won four straight on real margins. Over the last five games it scored more and allowed less than its season averages.

weekAhead.headline: Four home games against shaky defenses, without Curry and Green.
weekAhead.body:
All four games are at home, and three of the opponents rank 19th or lower on the site. Phoenix (29th, the league's worst DRtg at 126.3) and Miami (24th in defense) share a profile that suits Golden State: both protect the rim well but give up threes, at 43.9 and 40.5 percent. Phoenix is also the league's worst defensive-rebounding team, which sets up the Warriors' league-best offensive glass. Orlando brings a 24th-ranked offense and forces few turnovers, so the Warriors' ball security matters less there.

New Orleans closes the week and is the real test. Its defense ranks 13th and holds opponents to 30.5 percent from three, 5th in the league. It also gets to the line at the 4th-highest rate, which puts pressure on a frontcourt that cannot protect the rim. Without Curry the margins shrink, but this schedule should allow three wins; the Phoenix rematch and the New Orleans game decide whether it is more.

keyMatchups.title: Warriors shooters vs. porous perimeters
keyMatchups.body: Phoenix and Miami rank 30th and 29th in Opp 3P %, while sealing the paint well. That funnels games toward exactly what Golden State does best. Melton's 70.7 TS % and 19 threes make him the likeliest beneficiary with Curry out.

keyMatchups.title: Offensive glass vs. Phoenix
keyMatchups.body: The Warriors' league-leading ORB % meets a Phoenix team that ranks last in DRB % at 65.1. Phoenix won the first meeting 131-122, so second chances are the clearest edge in the rematch.

keyMatchups.title: New Orleans' defense and free throws
keyMatchups.body: The Pelicans take the fewest threes in the league but get to the line at the 4th-highest rate. Their frontcourt grades A-, against the Warriors' D-. Their perimeter defense blunts Golden State's main weapon, which makes this the week's toughest game.

weekAhead.watch: Whether Williams and Lendeborg can carry the creation load efficiently with Curry out, especially against New Orleans' perimeter defense.

restOfSeason.body:
The offense is the real thing in shape, if not quite in degree: three-point volume is a franchise trait, and the turnover-forcing should hold. The 40 percent from three and the league-leading offensive rebounding are likely to cool toward recent norms, which would pull the offensive rating into the 115 to 119 range. A defense allowing 73.1 at the rim will not improve on its own, and history says this group's defense has trended toward the middle of the league at best.

The result is a solid winning team rather than a contender, something like 42 to 48 wins with a Net Rtg between 0.5 and 4. That is a clear step up from last season's 37 wins, provided Curry's absence is short. A long one shifts the range toward the lower end and into play-in territory.
swingFactors: Length of Curry's and Green's absences
Any fix for the rim defense

confidence.note: Seven games, with two key players out and noisy on-off samples.
